Name: Artificial fill, undifferentiated
Description: Unconsolidated human-made deposits, predominantly consisting of piles of mining tailings of various ages in central part of map area
Label: af

Name: Alluvium
Description: Sand, silt, and gravel deposited by water in active stream channels, terraces, or valleys
Label: Qal

Name: Colluvium
Description: Angular gravel, cobbles, boulders, sand, and lesser silts deposited by transport of loose, unconsolidated material down hillslope
Label: Qc
GeoMaterial: Colluvium and other widespread mass-movement sediment

Name: Fluvial terrace deposits
Description: Well-rounded boulders, cobbles, and gravels along abandoned river terraces. Defined by geomorphic expression of planar surfaces or sets of surfaces and mapped using 1-meter (m)-resolution lidar. Internal contacts delineate individual terraces
Label: Qt

Name: Paleochannel deposits
Description: Sand, silt, and gravel deposits in abandoned stream channels. Identified on the basis of their geomorphic expression and incision into planar terraces. Mapped using lidar
Label: Qpc

Name: Landslide deposits
Description: Chaotic deposits of sand, silt, clay, angular boulders, and large bedrock blocks deposited by gravity-driven sliding and flow of material. Easily identified using lidar; primarily mapped on the basis of geomorphic expression. Arrows show direction of downslope movement. Internal contacts delineate individual landslides nested within larger landslides
Label: Qls
GeoMaterial: Debris flows, landslides, and other localized mass-movement sediment

Name: Older alluvium
Description: Sand, silt, and gravel in older alluvial deposits. Defined by relative age relations, lack of primary geomorphic expression, and highly dissected surfaces
Label: Qoal

Name: Travertine deposits
Description: White travertine deposits associated with springs near McLaughlin mine in central part of map area. Large siliceous sinter deposits were removed during excavation of McLaughlin gold deposit and are not mapped
Label: Qs

Name: Silica-carbonate
Description: Red to yellow to orange to white to black alteration zones of quartz, vitrified quartz, carbonate, magnesite, opal, chalcedony, pyrite, and lesser cinnabar. Formed during hydrothermal alteration of serpentinite; contains remnant serpentinite pieces. Rocks are intimately associated with gold and mercury deposits; exposures located near McLaughlin mine in central part of map area
Label: sc

Name: Lava flows
Description: Light-gray to black, porphyritic lava flows that range from olivine basalt to quartz-bearing dacite. Lavas typically fine grained, containing 5–10 percent phenocrysts as large as about 0.5 centimeters (cm) in diameter. Flows are resistant to erosion and form ridge tops and buttes. Most extensive exposures found along southwestern margin of map area and reach thicknesses of about 20 m. Whole-rock potassium-argon age of 2.2±0.2 mega-annum (Ma) on basaltic andesite (Lehman, 1986). Intercalated with units Qwt, Qpf, and Qva in different locations
Label: Qlv

Name: Welded tuff
Description: Light-gray to buff welded tuff that contains dark-gray fiamme as long as 5–10 cm and phenocrysts of plagioclase as large as 1 cm in diameter. Exposed in southwestern part of map area on ridge between Pope Creek and Putah Creek arm of Lake Berryessa. Intercalated with lava flows of unit Qlv
Label: Qwt

Name: Pumice-fall deposits
Description: White to pink to red pumice-fall deposits. Pumice clasts reach 5 cm in diameter and show variable clay alteration. Exposed on southeast side of hill south of McLaughlin open-pit mine. Stratigraphically overlain by lava flows of unit Qlv
Label: Qpf

Name: Altered volcanic rocks
Description: Light-tan to buff lava flows, dikes, and sills. Shows strong propylitic and argillic alteration (Tosdal and others, 1993) that is related to hydrothermal activity associated with McLaughlin mine ore body. Exposed near McLaughlin open-pit mine. Stratigraphically below ridge-capping lava flows of unit Qlv
Label: Qva

Name: Cache Formation
Description: Gray to light-gray, well-rounded fluvial gravels and lesser siltstone, sandstone, mudstone, and tuff. Gravel beds as thick as several meters have rare crossbedding and lenses of fine silts and sands. Clasts composed of metagraywacke, chert, vein quartz, schist, greenstone, and sandstone (Rymer, 1981). Lacustrine deposits locally contain plant and freshwater-fish fossils, ostracodes, pollen, and tephra layers (Rymer, 1981; Sims and others, 1981). Unit overlain by basalts (1.45 Ma); also contains obsidian pebbles derived from the Pliocene Sonoma Volcanics (4.5 Ma) (McLaughlin and others, 2018). Unit exposed in northwest corner of map area along Cache Creek; also includes fluvially reworked pumice deposits along Lake Berryessa (see Fox and others, 1973)
Label: QTc

Name: Venado Formation
Description: Thick-bedded to massive, fine- to coarse-grained quartz-biotite-lithic wacke and lesser mudstone, siltstone, and conglomerate; well indurated and ridge forming. Located in eastern part of map area along crest of Blue Ridge (see, for example, Graymer and others, 2002). Mudstones contain foraminifers of Late Cretaceous (Turonian) age (Goudkoff, 1945; Emerson and Roberts, 1962; Lachenbruch, 1962; Graymer and others, 2007)
Label: Kv

Name: Lower part of the Great Valley sequence
FullName: Lower part of the Great Valley sequence
Description:
Predominantly thin-bedded turbidite, dark-brown to grayish-brown shale, and tan, fine- to coarse-grained sandstone. Sandstone beds and channels are as thick as 1–2 m and are resistant to erosion, 
forming high ridges. Locally contains conglomerate layers traceable for several kilometers, 
carbonate lenses, and sandstone dikes. Unit is locally overturned adjacent to faults; up-direction 
indicators consist of Bouma sequences, ripple marks, flame structures, and load casts. Ridge-in-groove slickenlines along bedding surfaces suggest considerable bedding-parallel slip, although slip is difficult to map owing to lack of reliable offset markers. Our structural observations support work by Graymer and others (2007), who said many unrecognized faults likely exist and disrupt original stratigraphic sequence; tectonic mixing may be responsible for presence of Early Cretaceous and Late Jurassic Buchia spp. fossils in this unit (Weaver, 1949). Detrital zircon uranium-lead (U-Pb) ages between 133 and 144 Ma have been reported (McLaughlin and others, 2016; Orme and Surpless, 2019). Subdivided into the following:
Label: KJgvl

Name: Sedimentary serpentinite
Description: Teal-green to light-blue, coarse-grained serpentinite sand and detritus; angular fragments of serpentinite and ophiolitic debris as large as boulders. Outcrop patterns in map view form tabular to rounded bodies that appear to be concentrated in antiformal hinges and adjacent to faults, where rocks are highly sheared. North of map area, near Wilbur Springs, unit contains Early Cretaceous fossils (Carlson, 1984)
Label: KJssp

Name: Knoxville Formation
Description:
Dark-brown to dark-gray, thin-bedded turbidites that contain tan, fine- to medium-grained sandstone layers. Contains laterally discontinuous basalconglomerate lenses as thick as several meters. Locally overturned near faults. Unit is limited to rocks that contain Jurassic fossils and have Jurassic detrital-zircon ages; however, considerable faulting and deformation may have mixed Cretaceous and Jurassic rocks. Some structural complexities are too small to map, but other limiting factors are poor exposures and lack of dateable material to differentiate identical rocks that have different Cretaceous or Jurassic ages. Lower contact appears faulted everywhere, but timing of faulting unknown. Detrital zircon (U-Pb) ages are between 142 and 149 Ma (Orme and Surpless, 2019, supporting work of 
McLaughlin and others, 2016)
Label: Jk

Name: Ophiolitic-block mélange
Description:
Mélange consisting of blocks of ophiolitic affinity (that is, derived from the Coast Range ophiolite) in matrix of highly sheared sandstone, shale, argillite, serpentinite, and lesser sedimentary-serpentinite layers. Some ophiolitic blocks reach several hundred meters in diameter. Matrix is highly deformed and has densely spaced fracture and shear surfaces. Presence of well-rounded ophiolitic material in sandstone matrix, observed along north shore of Lake Berryessa (fig. 10), supports olistostrome origin originally proposed by Phipps (1984). Unit has undergone intensive shearing and tectonic mixing, but timing of deformation is unclear. McLaughlin and others (2018) estimated that tectonic mixing of 
similar ophiolitic-block mélange north of map area took place in Early Cretaceous (between 
Albian and Valanginian). Unit is stratigraphically below the Knoxville Formation in map area, 
although contact between units is laterally discontinuous and obscured by substantial faulting 
and dismemberment, making primary depositional relations difficult to decipher. Faulting has 
juxtaposed unit with the underlying Coast Range ophiolite, although contact exposures are poor 
and timing of faulting is unclear. Blocks within mélange include the following:
Label: Jom

Name: Pillow basalt
Description: Black to dark-brown, fine-grained pillow basalt that contains plagioclase phenocrysts. Pillows are tens of centimeters to 1 m in diameter; pillow asymmetries provide rare up-direction indicators
Label: ompb

Name: Basaltic rock
Description: Black to dark-brown to red basalt, mapped using aerial photographs and in field
Label: ombu

Name: Greenstone
Description: Dark-green to black, fine-grained greenstone
Label: omgs

Name: Serpentinite
Description: Green to teal-green serpentinite
Label: omsp

Name: Ophiolitic blocks, undifferentiated
Description: Mapped from geomorphic expression using aerial photographs only; not field checked. Internal contacts outline individual blocks that appear to be in contact
Label: omu

Name: Breccia of Pope Creek
Description:
Black to dark-gray, mafic breccia that also contains clasts of 
lesser gabbro and tuff. Located along Pope Creek in southwest corner of map area. McLaughlin 
and others (2016) determined U-Pb age of 151.1±2.5 Ma from zircons in overlying tuff at Pope 
Creek locality, suggesting that breccia is coeval with rocks of Elder Creek terrane near Paskenta. 
Unit possibly correlates to the basaltic breccia unit mvbb, notably at Jim Dollar Mountain in 
central part of map area
Label: Jobb

Name: Serpentinized ultramafic rocks
Description: Tectonically sheared serpentinite-matrix mélange and massive, serpentinized harzburgite. Texture is well jointed and consists of brecciated blocks within a highly sheared, matrix-rich monomict serpentinite mélange (Melosh, 2019). Slabs and blocks of ophiolitic affinity that are tectonically entrained within mélange include basalt, gabbro, amphibolite, tuffaceous chert, tuff, and plagiogranite, as well as pieces of sandstone and shale from the Great Valley sequence. Uranium-lead (U-Pb) age of 163.6±2.0 Ma on zircon in plagiogranite (unit pgb) block (Orme and Surpless, 2019). Blocks within mélange include the following:
Label: Josp

Name: Massive serpentinite
Description: Dark- to light-green, massive serpentinite, weathers to orange and red. Chrysotile-filled joints surround serpentinite kernels and brecciated kernels. Unit shows little to no shear deformation, although it may contain discrete shear zones; blocks reach several kilometers in diameter
Label: msp

Name: Amphibolite
Description: Black, medium- to fine-grained amphibolite that contains hornblende, biotite, muscovite, and lesser chlorite. Contains ductily deformed quartz ribbons that have bulging recrystallization textures
Label: ab
GeoMaterial: Medium and high-grade regional metamorphic rock, of unspecified origin

Name: Schist
Description: Mica schist blocks consisting of white and dark-gray to black to light-orange muscovite and biotite schists and fine-grained plagioclase and quartz
Label: shb
GeoMaterial: Medium and high-grade regional metamorphic rock, of unspecified origin

Name: Chert
Description: Brown to white, well-bedded chert containing abundant radiolaria that are visible in thin section
Label: cb

Name: Basaltic breccia
Description:
Black to dark-brown, clast-supported basaltic breccia. Basalt has fine-grained 
porphyritic texture and contains phenocrysts of plagioclase and olivine alteration products, 
including chlorite and epidote. Likely correlative with the breccia of Pope Creek (Jobb)
Label: mvbb

Name: Pillow basalt
Description: Black to dark-brown, fine-grained pillow basalt that contains plagioclase phenocrysts. Pillows are tens of centimeters to 1 m in diameter; pillow asymmetries provide rare up-direction indicators
Label: mvpb

Name: Basalt, undifferentiated
Description: Black to dark-brown to red basalt, mapped using aerial photographs and in field
Label: mvbu

Name: Plagiogranite
Description: White to buff, porphyritic plagiogranite that contains phenocrysts of quartz and plagioclase as large as 1–2 cm in diameter; dated at 163.6±2.0 Ma (Orme and Surpless, 2019)
Label: pgb

Name: Gabbro and cumulate gabbro
Description: Dark-gray to black, porphyritic gabbro that contains phenocrysts of plagioclase, amphibole, and pyroxene 0.5 cm in diameter. Some blocks show cumulate layering textures
Label: gb

Name: Sandstone and mudstone
Description: Gray to light-brown, medium- to coarse-grained sandstone and dark-brown mudstone
Label: ssb

Name: Tuff
Description: Gray to greenish-gray to white tuff; bubble-wall shards visible in thin section
Label: tfb

Name: Metagraywake
Description: Light-brown to gray to dark-gray, coarse- to fine-grained, lawsonite- and jadeite-bearing metagraywacke and schist that has metamorphic foliation and textural zone 2A fabrics (Jayko and others, 1986). Similar rocks outside map area have radiometric metamorphic ages of 90–110 Ma (Mattinson and Echeverria, 1980; Wakabayashi, 1999), and they contain Late Jurassic fossils (Crawford, 1976). Unit may be correlative with rocks of Yolla Bolly terrane farther north (see, for example, McLaughlin and Ohlin, 1984)
Label: Kfm

Name: Lake
Description: Water
Label: Lake
